newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania shilling weakens on dollar, pound.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania shilling weakens on dollar, pound.

text.p: The Tanzania shilling weakened against the dollar and pound on Friday, central bank (BoT) figures showed.
The shilling traded at a mean rate of 590.4360 versus the dollar from Thursday's 590.4261. Against the pound, the shilling traded at a mean rate 922.0278 from 921.6581 on Thursday.
Dealers said they expected the shilling to remain stable, within a 590-596 dollar band, for the next two to three months. They also noted BoT dollar purchases on the market.
"I really don't see any chance of large movements against the dollar. The BoT is quite happy where the shilling is right now," one dealer told Reuters.
"We certainly don't see much chance of the rate moving wildly like we saw six months ago," the dealer said.

Another dealer said the current surplus of dollars in the market was likely to continue as Tanzania was on target to get an International Monetary Fund (IMF) soft-lending Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility loan (ESAF) by October.
Export proceeds would also add to the surplus, he said.
Volatility this week on the shilling-pound market was due to an almost total absence of any major deals being done in sterling, dealers said.
"Everyone trades in dollars in this market. One (pound) transaction can cause wild fluctuations because nobody really trades in shillings-pounds," he said.

Dealers said the market took allegations of a recent tax evasion scam involving finance minister Simon Mbilinyi in stride. A government report this week censured Mbilinyi for acting improperly in waiving import duties on an edible oil shipment.
